summary_paragraph: A male patient, status post orthotopic liver transplant, was admitted for evaluation of elevated liver enzymes and new-onset tremors. A liver biopsy was performed, which ruled out rejection but showed neutrophilic inflammation. An ERCP revealed a biliary stricture at the anastomosis, which was treated with sphincterotomy and placement of two biliary stents. His liver function tests subsequently improved. He developed hyperkalemia, managed with kayexalate, fludrocortisone, and low-dose furosemide. Neurological evaluation for abnormal involuntary movements, including head shaking and facial grimacing, found no acute intracranial or spinal cord abnormalities on MRI; the movements resolved, and a psychological component was considered. An EGD showed only mild gastropathy. The patient stabilized, resumed oral intake, and was discharged home with family support, visiting nurse services, and a plan for weekly lab monitoring.
